scope: Read-only wrapper, lane-aligner and previously reviewed CDC integration reasoning, plus inspection of current port oracle and fault definitions. All eight frozen inputs rehashed; no execution of the recovered-x4 tests/native/formal campaign. Runtime-controller code not independently audited here.

findings.subject: Lane wiring and complete records
findings.reason: Generate lane0..3 uses exactly that recovered clock, raw_i[lane*32+:32], control and force-realign bit. The same lane feeds its own FIFO writer and common-clock reader. Each complete output occupies disjoint194-bit block and3-bit length slices plus independent SKP/EIEOS/realign bits; all776 block and12 length bits are covered. No lane swap, truncation or metadata collapse found.

findings.subject: Registered aligner-to-FIFO interface
findings.reason: The aligner produces registered block_valid/data/metadata. FIFO write logic on the same recovered edge consumes the previous registered bundle, preserving atomicity with one-edge latency. The FIFO accepts unthrottleable valid input or latches overflow; wr_accept_o is intentionally not used as upstream backpressure.

findings.subject: Reset and stopped clocks
findings.reason: Clean por/reset level resets both domains of each FIFO. Release uses the existing three-stage local synchronization, boot and peer-ready handshake. lane_running holds the aligner synchronous reset while its clock is stopped or the FIFO is not ready. A stale aligner valid cannot be accepted while wr_running is false, and resumed edges clear it before the running barrier releases. Global active also requires all four common-domain running flags, so one stopped lane prevents common output startup.

findings.subject: Fault propagation and epoch abort
findings.reason: Only each FIFO synchronized common-domain rd_fault contributes to fault_o; no raw recovered-domain loss/fault drives the common data barrier. A local sticky write fault stops that lane and remains until coordinated reset. fault_o masks all lane valid and all FIFO read-ready, preserving all-or-nothing output epoch invalidation after synchronization. Other lanes may keep receiving and eventually fault too while reset is pending; there is no automatic partial-lane restart.

findings.subject: Held output and buffering
findings.reason: Each lane valid is active AND common_valid, and the matching FIFO ready is active AND that lane ready_i. Thus stalled records stay owned by their FIFO while other lanes may retire independently. Reset or synchronized global fault intentionally invalidates held outputs; downstream must discard the epoch. Before the fault crosses, a previously valid buffered prefix may retire as the source comments already state.

findings.subject: Port oracle scope
findings.reason: Current oracle serializes independent lane-specific payloads, all five SKP lengths and EIEOS; compares each valid lane slice rather than converting unrelated invalid X bits. Eight phase iterations distribute offsets0..31 across four lanes; this is not all32 offsets independently repeated on every lane. Source includes stall, one-lane loss/overflow, explicit force-realign, stopped-clock startup and held-reset cases, plus nine actual wiring-mutation definitions and two invalid depths. This peer did not execute them.

scope_notes: active_o denotes all CDC readers running, not all lanes aligned or deskewed. Valid records remain four independent ordered streams.
lane_running_o, lane_aligned_o and lane_fault_o remain recovered-domain diagnostics; common-domain logic should use active_o/fault_o or synchronize diagnostics separately.

Search-triggered EIEOS realignment is preserved realign metadata and does not itself assert a global fault. Explicit force_realign on an aligned lane produces loss through the frozen aligner. Downstream MAC/deskew must interpret metadata/control epochs; no silent assumption of a deskewed packet stream is valid.
No full PCS/PHY, rate-compensation, physical Gray-pointer constraints, reset recovery/removal, metastability/MTBF, skew-tolerance or end-to-end sustained controller qualification.
